A_general.open_code_note: The public repository is Xero’s local stdio developer server. Xero describes the Claude connector as a separate read-only connection; the repository exposes a broader set of read/write commands. The hosted input endpoint’s implementation is not public.
A_general.release_status: NOT FOUND for the input endpoint
other_official_servers: https://api.xero.com/mcp/v1 — Xero Developer Remote MCP, documented for developers and builders; GA, with 39 documented tools and read/write operations.
XeroAPI/xero-mcp-server — public local stdio server; its README lists 51 commands, including read, create, update, approve, revert, and delete operations.

B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: Xero says the Claude connector is free to add and available to organisations on any Xero business pricing plan; an active Xero subscription and a Claude account are required. No separate connector fee is stated.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: Prices vary by country. The official US pricing update effective October 1, 2026 lists Early at $27/month, Growing at $59/month, and Established at $97/month, USD before tax.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: The connector is free to add; the linked Xero subscription is paid. The cited US prices are regional and may change.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: Sign-in and user approval are required. Xero Central says the Claude connector connects to one Xero organisation at a time; changing organisations requires disconnecting and reconnecting.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Xero controls connector availability and its access model; the end user selects and authorises the organisation; access also requires an eligible Xero subscription and Claude account.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. Xero describes the input connector as read-only; its 20 listed tools are retrieval/reporting operations. The listing gives no tool annotations. 2. No server-enforced confirmation mechanism is documented for this read-only endpoint. For the separate Developer Remote MCP, Xero says V1 tools do not elicit confirmation and recommends that the client ask before writes. 3. The supplied metadata lists OAuth scopes; Xero says the connector accesses a selected organisation after sign-in and approval. The listing says one organisation at a time. Endpoint-specific inheritance of user roles, admin switches, token lifetime, and redirect approval are Unknown. 4. No read/write mode switch, tool filter, or endpoint-specific region/environment mode was found. 5. Xero says connector data is used to answer questions and is not stored between sessions; Xero also says the data is not used to train Claude. Field masking and PII exclusions are Unknown. 6. Endpoint-specific rate limits, result caps, and call costs are Unknown. 7. Parameter validation/correction is Unknown; tool schemas were not published. 8. Endpoint-specific logging and telemetry are Unknown. Xero’s separate developer endpoint logs API calls, not prompts or MCP tool calls. 9. No feedback, rating, reporting, survey, or upsell tool appears in the listed 20 names. 10. No endpoint-supplied skills or initialize instructions were found. 11. Xero says retrieved data is not stored between sessions; effects of within-session history are Unknown. 12. The input endpoint presents one flat listed tool set. 13. No raw API, SQL, script, or arbitrary request tool appears in the listed names.
D_server_side_logic.server_structure_explanation: The evidence for the input endpoint shows one hosted endpoint and one flat list of 20 tools. Xero’s separate developer endpoint and local stdio repository are documented separately.

E_aggregated.action_count_comment: No official Xero tool reference for this endpoint was found. The Claude connector directory lists 20 tools and marks the listing Anthropic verified and Made by Xero Limited; under the source rules, its names are treated as third-party evidence. The separate Xero Developer Remote MCP documentation lists 39 tools, and the public local stdio README lists 51 commands; neither list is included because those are different server variants. The mcpservers.org catalogue confirms the endpoint but supplies no tool count or individual names. Agent Discoverability reports 20 tools for a ChatGPT plugin, a separate surface; Composio’s 53-tool listing is a proxy/API toolkit and was not used as endpoint evidence. No catalogue-only actions were added.

E_aggregated.token_method: Tool definitions and initialize instructions for the input endpoint were not published verbatim. The available public repository is a different local server variant, so its token count does not represent the input endpoint.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: The connector is read-only, so the agent cannot change Xero records through these tools. A human can change records in Xero; for example, Xero’s product documentation describes sending invoices and quotes and managing bills. Sources: https://www.xero.com/us/pricing-plans/update/ and https://central.xero.com/0/article/Connect-Xero-using-the-Xero-connector-in-Claude

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: Xero Central advises: “To help you get better answers, your prompt should include a clear business question, a time period or a customer name.” This is guidance to users; no endpoint code or enforcement mechanism was found.
F_documentation.governance_promises: Xero Central states: “Your Xero data isn’t used to train Claude’s AI model.” The Claude connector listing says: “Any data retrieved is used only to respond to your questions and is never stored between sessions.”
F_documentation.promises_to_user: Xero describes the Claude connector as read-only and says responses can link back to the Xero report, invoice, or contact used. Xero’s product page says users remain in control of decisions.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: Read-only access is consistent with the listed retrieval/reporting tools, but the hosted implementation is closed and its enforcement cannot be independently inspected. The data-use and retention statements are documentation promises; no endpoint code was available to verify them.

contradictions: The supplied protected-resource metadata for `https://mcp.xero.com/mcp` lists `accounting.settings`, `accounting.invoices.read`, and three report-read scopes, while the connector’s 20 tools also cover contacts, bills, repeating invoices, tracking categories, purchase orders, bank transactions, 1099 summaries, and connected organisations. The metadata’s `scopes_supported` is not proof of the scopes actually granted to a user, so the mismatch does not establish that those tools are inaccessible.

The Claude connector listing and Xero Central describe `mcp.xero.com/mcp` as read-only. Xero’s separate Developer Remote MCP at `api.xero.com/mcp/v1` is documented as read/write with 39 tools; these are distinct endpoints and tool sets.

The public XeroAPI repository is a local stdio server whose README lists 51 commands, including write and delete operations. It is not the deployed implementation of the input endpoint and its tools are excluded from `actions.json`.
observations_for_research: Xero operates distinct MCP surfaces under the same product name: the Claude connector is read-only and limited to one organisation at a time, while the developer remote endpoint supports read/write operations and multiple authorised organisations.
The input endpoint publishes OAuth metadata with a scope list that does not map transparently to the full set of named connector tools.
